dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the incident report and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The system diagrams review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Council technical briefings with prepared slides go consistently well.
Prepared public speaking is proven.
Proven across years of budget seasons.
Someone new shadowed me in the utility office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the public statements into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My prepared formats carry the public-facing record: council briefings, written summaries, and the annual open-house presentations have all run clean for six years.
Six clean years across prepared formats.
Six years without a correction.
Written incident summaries for the public record draw praise from the regulator.
The written channel is strong.
Strong and audited.
I archived last cycle's notes on the system diagrams and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
A media-training course with simulated live press conferences is booked for next quarter, my first formal training of that kind.
A proper measurement instrument is scheduled.
Scheduled and paid for.
A vendor call about the incident report ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the utility office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the public statements.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the system diagrams records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
My only live press conference was the boil-notice night: no communications support, a failing microphone, and shouted questions, and the coverage called the utility's response confused.
One chaotic sample under broken conditions.
Broken enough to measure the venue, not me.
I sketched next week's plan for the public statements before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the incident report updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The communications director must file the utility's spokesperson roster this month, before the training happens.
The roster deadline precedes the measurement.
That is the whole tension.
The director says listing a backup spokesperson looks indecisive to the board.
Optics pressure on a measurement question.
Optics versus data, as usual.
I closed the week by updating the utility office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The communications director asked whether to list me as primary press spokesperson this year. Realistically, what should I tell her right now?
